description: The tri-api vector corpus and the Python model's answer for each. Bytes are latin-1 strings. The compiled Zig's answers are recorded in tri_api_zig.json; the specs' decision functions are replayed against cases derived from these records (`replay`).

vectors.note: an empty string value reads as absent
the raw escaped text is returned, not the decoded value
one space after the colon and the key is not found
a numeric value is never read: only quoted strings are
the same number as a string is read
no closing quote: the value runs to the end of the data
the needle ends the data: nothing to read
the first textual match wins, nested or not
a doubled backslash before a quote is taken as an escaped quote
multi-byte text is handled byte for byte
provider usage as JSON numbers reads as 0 and 0
a space after the colon makes stop_reason default to end_turn

in.body: this is not json at all

vectors.note: a body that is not JSON yields nothing and no error
a provider error object yields no blocks
a tool_use without an id is named unknown
a nested type:text inside a tool input is read as a text block
a text block longer than the 8192-byte window is cut
max_tokens read as the stop reason
a tool_use block whose own second `type` key precedes any brace makes the scan spin forever (measured on the binary, not run here)
DEL and high bytes pass through raw
braces inside strings do not count
a string value is not an object
whitespace before the brace is skipped
the pattern is everything between the first ( and the last )
an MCP name carries a dot
an empty pattern matches every argument
prefix: the star is only honoured as the last byte
two spaces escape a prefix rule
the argument is shorter than the prefix
a star in the middle is a literal
an MCP call is checked with an empty argument, so a prefix rule never matches
only * or empty can allow or deny an MCP tool
an unknown tool defaults to deny
a deny rule can close a default-allow tool
an MCP tool defaults to deny
an MCP tool with an allow rule
an MCP allow with a restricting pattern never matches
an MCP deny with a restricting pattern never matches either
a space after the colon finds no array and loads no rule
the needle is exactly "allow":[ with no space
a ] inside a rule string does not end the array
a string that is not a rule is skipped
only the first 64 rules are kept; the rest are dropped without a word
an escaped quote inside a rule splits it
the first occurrence of the needle wins
so is a path into a home directory
a file name containing two dots is refused
an escaped dot is not seen as a dot
a longer word is not bare ls
pwd has no trailing space, so pwdx is a prefix match
an escaped newline is text, not a newline
a short AKIA token of nine bytes is NOT redacted
the token ends at the quote
an empty text is one token
fewer than three assistant turns: nothing is truncated
five turns: results before the last three are cut
short results are kept even before the cut
a result of exactly 200 bytes is kept, 201 is cut
no assistant turn: the whole history, the first prompt included, becomes the summary
two turns: still everything is summarised
five turns: the last three are kept verbatim, the first prompt is not
